description.fun: Mudkip is small but mighty, strong enough to shove or crush boulders bigger than itself, and it's been seen trying to crush rocks even in its sleep. The fin on its head senses currents in the air and water, and it sleeps buried in the mud at the water's edge. Online it starred in the 'so i herd u liek mudkipz' meme, which Pokémon Trading Card Game Live later nodded to.
description.guide: A small Water-type amphibian Pokémon and one of Hoenn's three first partners. The fin on its head senses water and air currents, and it is strong enough to crush boulders. It evolves into Marshtomp and then Swampert.
description.tagline: A tiny, boulder-crushing mudskipper and an internet favourite

description.fun: Marshtomp is coated in a thin, sticky film that lets it live on land, and it's actually faster in mud than in water, with sturdy legs that keep their footing where opponents slip. If its skin dries out it weakens, so it plays in the beach mud at low tide to top up. The fin on its head resembles a Roman gladiator's crested helmet.
description.guide: A Water- and Ground-type amphibian Pokémon, the middle stage of the Mudkip line. A sticky film on its skin lets it live on land, and it moves faster through mud than water. It evolves into Swampert at level 36.
description.tagline: A mud-loving amphibian that's fastest in the muck

description.fun: Swampert can drag a boulder of more than a ton, swim faster than a jet ski and even tow a large ship. Its fins pick up subtle changes in the waves and wind, so it senses storms coming and piles up boulders to protect its nest. It coats itself in mud to keep its skin moist, and its hunched stance recalls a sumo wrestler.
description.guide: A large Water- and Ground-type amphibian Pokémon, the final form of Mudkip. It is very strong, with arms harder than rock, and its fins can sense approaching storms. It can Mega Evolve into Mega Swampert.
description.tagline: A mud-caked powerhouse that can tow a ship and sense storms

description.fun: Mega Swampert bulks up hugely, with the water in its body powering its muscles like a hydraulic pump, so it can stand on two legs and throw heavy punches on land or in water. Its look may borrow from scuba diving.
